ledger.title: reboot_reconcile matches the journal's UPSTOX-space `trading_symbol` against a NOREN-keyed position book, so EVERY open position always reads "flat" and is false-closed on the first non-empty book read
ledger.evidence:
`backend/app/live/reboot_reconcile.py:143` reads the flat/held key from the wrong symbol space:

```python
tsym = str(doc.get("trading_symbol") or "")
if tsym in open_tsyms:      # open_tsyms is built from NOREN position_book rows
    summary["skipped_held"] += 1
    continue
```

`open_tsyms` comes from `_open_tsyms(book)` (`reboot_reconcile.py:58-75`), keyed on the broker row's `tsym` — Noren space (`NIFTY18AUG26P24300`). But the journal doc's `trading_symbol` is UPSTOX space. `backend/app/auto_live.py:576-581` writes both fields and labels them explicitly:

```python
"trading_symbol": contract_doc.get("trading_symbol") or "",
# UPSTOX-space above; the broker's own symbol + segment below. Joining the
# two spaces is a long-standing source of real bugs here, so both are
# stored explicitly rather than inferred at read time.
"noren_tsym": result.get("tsym") or "",
```

`backend/app/live/flattrade_symbol.py:21` confirms `trading_symbol` is the "Upstox symbol (not the Noren tsym)". The rest of the codebase already treats this join as forbidden — `backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:601-603` ("NEVER on trading_symbol — live_trades stores the UPSTOX symbol while the position book is NOREN-keyed"), `backend/app/runtime.py:722-724`, and `backend/app/live/ownership.py:22-24`. The identical bug was already found and fixed in the blotter at `backend/app/live/live_blotter.py:113-117`: "matching on it never succeeded and every live trade rendered as not-held". `reboot_reconcile.py:143` is the one place that was never fixed.

The lookup can therefore NEVER hit, so `tsym in open_tsyms` is always False and every non-CLOSED doc falls straight through to `close_live_trade(..., exit_reason="reconciled_closed")` at `reboot_reconcile.py:149-158`. The empty-book UNKNOWN guard (`reboot_reconcile.py:300-304`) is the ONLY thing that was holding the position — which is exactly why the logs show many benign "position_book empty/None — treating as UNKNOWN" passes and then a single destructive pass the moment a real book arrived.

This also explains `realized_pnl=null`: `_match_exit_fill_price` (`reboot_reconcile.py:89-115`) is passed the same UPSTOX `tsym`, so its same-tsym SELL fallback also cannot match, it returns None, and `close_live_trade` closes the doc without a price (`backend/app/live/close_loop.py:100-101`, `144`).

The path is not boot-only. `backend/app/runtime.py:777-778` sets `complete=False` on `unknown_position_book`, `maybe_run_live_recovery` refuses to latch success (`runtime.py:824-835`), and the supervisor re-invokes it every tick (`runtime.py:1240`); the OAuth callback also forces a run (`backend/app/routers/live_broker.py:512`). So it retried through the session and fired mid-market at the first readable book.

The test suite is blind to this: every fixture in `tests/test_reboot_reconcile.py` uses the SAME string for both spaces (`tests/test_reboot_reconcile.py:165` `"trading_symbol": "NIFTY24X25000CE"` vs book `{"tsym": "NIFTY24X25000CE"}` at `:244`), and not one fixture sets `noren_tsym`.
ledger.failure: Today, 2026-08-14: BUY NIFTY18AUG26P24300 qty 65 filled at 61.70. The doc held `trading_symbol` = the Upstox symbol and `noren_tsym` = `NIFTY18AUG26P24300`. At 05:14:38Z the broker returned a non-empty position_book that DID contain `{tsym: "NIFTY18AUG26P24300", netqty: 65}`. Reconcile looked up the Upstox string in a Noren-keyed map, missed, concluded "flat at the broker", and closed the row: status=CLOSED, exit_reason="reconciled_closed", realized_pnl=null — while the broker held netqty=65 for ~30 more minutes. Because the row is no longer OPEN its unrealized P&L is not summed, and because realized_pnl is null no loss is counted, so `max_concurrent` and the daily loss cap both went blind to a real, live, losing position. I reproduced this against the repo's own harness with the real trade's shape and the broker still holding 65: `summary={'closed': 1, ..., 'status': 'ok', 'close_detail': {'closed': 1, 'skipped_held': 0, ...}}`, `status=CLOSED`, `exit_reason=reconciled_closed`, `realized_pnl=None`, `exit_price=None` — a byte-for-byte match to the production log line and journal row.
ledger.proposed_fix:
Minimal root-cause fix in `_reconcile_open_flat` (`backend/app/live/reboot_reconcile.py:143`): resolve the held/flat key in BROKER space only, and fail CLOSED when it is unavailable.

```python
# The position book is NOREN-keyed. `trading_symbol` is UPSTOX-space; comparing
# the two made every OPEN doc read "flat" and false-closed live positions
# (2026-08-14). NO fallback to trading_symbol — unlike live_blotter (display
# only), a wrong answer here is an irreversible close.
tsym = str(doc.get("noren_tsym") or "").strip()
if not tsym:
    summary["skipped_unknown_symbol"] += 1   # legacy row: cannot prove flat -> HOLD
    continue
if tsym in open_tsyms:
    summary["skipped_held"] += 1
    continue
```

and pass that same `tsym` into `_match_exit_fill_price` (already the case at line 150, so it is fixed by the same change). Add `skipped_unknown_symbol` to the summary and log it at WARNING so legacy rows are visible rather than silently immortal. For legacy docs the broker-space symbol is recoverable without a fallback guess: `live_orders` `intent.tsym` IS the Noren symbol that was POSTed and survives overnight (`backend/app/live/ownership.py:14-24`), so look it up by `norenordno` before giving up.

I validated this patch against three cases with the repo's harness: (1) today's real trade with the broker still holding 65 -> stays OPEN, `skipped_held=1`; (2) a genuine PC-down exit (SELL fill tagged `oco:<norenordno>` at 80.0, flat book) -> still CLOSED with `realized_pnl=1189.5` = 65*(80-61.70), so the module's actual purpose is preserved; (3) a legacy doc with no `noren_tsym` -> stays OPEN, `skipped_unknown_symbol=1`. All three pass.

Also fix the mirrored fixtures: `tests/test_reboot_reconcile.py:161-173` `_open_doc()` must set `noren_tsym` to a string DIFFERENT from `trading_symbol`, so the two spaces can never silently collapse again.

ledger.title: The OCO stop leg is transmitted and fires INSTANTLY at placement — x/y direction is inverted, so the 'resting backstop' can never rest
ledger.evidence:
Broker order book read live today (mcp__flattrade__get_order_book):
  norenordno 26081400076294  B 65 NIFTY18AUG26P24300 @61.70 COMPLETE  remarks="ee334051647948068397d0250647360b" (the cid)
  norenordno 26081400076303  S 65 @prc=21.00 REJECTED
     remarks = "LMT_BOS_O: oco:26081400076294: Ltp 61.95 is above 21.45: oco:26081400076294"
     rejreason = "RED:Margin Shortfall:INR 101830.33 Available:INR 86932.68 for C-FZ08714 [KAMBALA]"
The leg order number (…076303) is 9 ids after the entry (…076294) — it was created seconds after the fill, NOT at a trigger. The broker's own remark states why: it compared LTP 61.95 against the x trigger 21.45 and evaluated "is ABOVE" as TRUE, so it fired leg1 immediately.

The numbers reconcile exactly with our code. backend/app/live/oco_levels.py:37-53 with entry 61.35 and guard_stop_pct≈50: eff = max(50, 50+MIN_GAP_PP=15) = 65 → sl_trigger = round_down(61.35*0.35) = 21.45, sl_limit = round_down(21.45*0.98) = 21.00. Those are precisely the 21.45/21.00 in the broker remark.

The assumption that broke is documented as CONFIRMED but is wrong: backend/app/live/gtt.py:74-79 — "oivariable var 'x' pairs positionally with place_order_params (leg1) … the broker infers above/below from each trigger value vs the LTP — so leg direction is value-driven, not x/y-labelled." The live remark proves x is an ABOVE comparison regardless of value. backend/app/live/gtt.py:307-309 puts sl_trigger (always BELOW entry, by construction in oco_levels.py:50) into x, so the condition "LTP above sl_trigger" is TRUE the instant it is placed, every single time.

Also falsified: gtt.py:5-14 claims a GTT "blocks NO margin and only fires a real order once its trigger price is hit … IMMUNE to the naked-short margin trap." The fired leg is an ordinary order and was margin-checked and rejected — the exact trap backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:4-10 says was already proven live on 2026-06-24 ("the broker SL backstop is REJECTED every time and the position is left unprotected").
ledger.failure: Every deployed live entry places an OCO whose SL leg fires immediately. Two branches, both bad: (a) the account lacks naked-short SPAN margin (what happened at 10:31 today) → the leg is REJECTED, the OCO is consumed, and there is NO broker backstop for any deployed position, ever — the PC-down net advertised in live_deploy_context.py:88-93 does not exist for a single trade; (b) if margin WERE available, a SELL LMT @21.00 against a 61.95 bid is a marketable limit and executes immediately at ~61.9 — the position would be flattened at break-even seconds after entry while the app still believes it is holding (the guard registry, journal and blotter all show OPEN). Today only the margin shortfall prevented branch (b).
ledger.proposed_fix: Stop emitting the current shape — it has no correct outcome. Either (1) prove the pairing by readback before trusting it: place nothing until one OCO is confirmed via GetPendingGTTOrder (docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/19-get-pending-gtt-order.md) with its stored oivariable direction, and correct gtt.py:307-309 to whichever var is the below/stop side (likely y for a long-option protective stop, with x carrying the above/target trigger); or (2) if the account can never carry naked-short SPAN for the fired leg — which live_position_guard.py:4-10 says is the standing reality for this option-buyer account — delete the OCO block from live_deploy_context.py:167-219 entirely and journal every deployed position as software-guard-only, so nothing anywhere claims a PC-down net. Do NOT keep it as a silent best-effort: it currently produces a false 'protected' badge with zero protection. Correct the gtt.py:5-14 and :74-79 docstrings, which now assert the opposite of measured broker behaviour.

ledger.title: A rejected OCO is journalled as successful — oco_error is derived from the presence of an alert id, and nothing ever reads back whether the backstop exists
ledger.evidence:
The exact swallow path, in order:
1. backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:375-381 place_oco → _post_alert (:419-432) → _parse_alert_response (:482-502). Line 501: `ok = al_id is not None and str(stat).strip().lower() != "not_ok"`. The broker returned the DOCUMENTED SUCCESS for PlaceOCOOrder — stat "OI created" + al_id (docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md:97,102-109,128) — so ok=True is *correct at that layer*: the ALERT was created. What was rejected is the ORDER the alert fired, a different object with its own status, in a different book.
2. backend/app/live_deploy_context.py:193-204. It DOES check `if res.get("ok")` (:195) — so a stat-level Not_Ok would be caught, and the try/except at :212-217 is not what hid this (place_oco already converts transport RuntimeError into ok=False at flattrade_client.py:428-431). The hole is structural: line 196 `oco_al_id = res.get("al_id")` is the LAST word. There is no GetPendingGTTOrder readback, and no scan of the order book for a leg carrying remarks `oco:<norenordno>` — even though live_deploy_context.py:191 stamps exactly that join key onto the OCO (`remarks=f"oco:{norenordno}"`) and the broker echoed it back verbatim today.
3. backend/app/auto_live.py:591-592:
     "oco_al_id": result.get("oco_al_id"),
     "oco_error": None if result.get("oco_al_id") else "no_broker_backstop",
   The journal's ONLY definition of failure is 'no id'. An id that came back from a placement whose leg was rejected 9 order-numbers later ⇒ oco_error=None ⇒ 'protected' to every consumer.
Note the app already owns the verification primitive it never calls at arm time: FlattradeClient.gtt_book() (flattrade_client.py:395-406) is used by reboot_reconcile.py:319 and routers/live_broker.py:1344, just never here.
ledger.failure: live_trades row for the 2026-08-14 NIFTY18AUG26P24300 entry carries oco_al_id="26081400000991", oco_error=null. The broker book carries the matching leg REJECTED for margin shortfall. The journal is the system of record for every downstream backstop decision, so a position with zero broker-side protection is recorded, displayed, and reasoned about as PC-down protected — for the whole life of the trade and forever afterwards in the journal.
ledger.proposed_fix: Make the journal record broker truth, not placement acknowledgement. In live_deploy_context.py after :196, before returning the id: (a) read gtt_book() and require a row whose al_id matches AND whose tsym matches; and/or (b) read order_book() and reject the id if any row has remarks containing `oco:{norenordno}` with status REJECTED/CANCELED. Only then return oco_al_id; otherwise return None so auto_live journals "no_broker_backstop" as designed. Because the leg can be rejected asynchronously, also carry the verification into the guard cycle (re-assert once, a few seconds after arm) rather than only at arm. Widen the journal field from a boolean-ish pair to a status the truth can be written into (e.g. oco_state ∈ {verified_resting, place_ack_only, rejected:<rejreason>, absent}) and store the broker's rejreason verbatim. This adds no arming/qualification gate — the entry still fills and the software guard still registers first (live_deploy_context.py:146-163); only the recorded claim changes.
ledger.note: The BLOCKER, and the root of this whole session: oco_error was derived from the presence of an al_id, so an ACCEPTED-then-asynchronously-REJECTED OCO journalled as protected while the GTT book was empty. Fixed ac1c03a: oco_verify.unbacked_norenordnos() re-checks every claimed al_id against the live GTT book each 10s supervisor tick and clears phantoms to no_broker_backstop (gtt_book=None => UNKNOWN => no action, so a transient read failure cannot destroy a real handle). Lights the existing software-guard-only alert rail.

ledger.title: The rejected "S 65 @prc=21.00" is provably AlphaForge's own OCO stop leg — and it was priced off the REFERENCE (61.35), not the fill (61.70)
ledger.evidence: Reproduced exactly, from the shipped code: `python -c "from app.live.oco_levels import compute_catastrophe_band; print(compute_catastrophe_band(61.35, guard_stop_pct=50.0))"` → **(21.45, 21.00, 144.15, 141.25)**. sl_limit == **21.00** == the rejected order's price. From the FILL (61.70) the same call returns (21.55, **21.10**, 144.95, 142.05) — a different price that does not appear in the order book. Chain: `backend/app/live_deploy_context.py:152` registers `entry_price=float(ref_ltp)` (→ guard stop_level 30.68 = 61.35×0.5 ⇒ guard_stop_pct resolves to exactly 50.0 at `live_deploy_context.py:143-145`); `live_deploy_context.py:174-179` then calls `compute_catastrophe_band(float(ref_ltp), guard_stop_pct=...)`; `backend/app/live/oco_levels.py:40-53` computes eff = max(50, 50+15) = 65 → sl_trigger = 61.35×0.35 = 21.4725 → tick-down 21.45, sl_limit = 21.45×0.98 = 21.021 → tick-down 21.00. `live_deploy_context.py:191` sets `remarks=f"oco:{norenordno}"`, and `backend/app/live/gtt.py:243-244` copies that remark onto BOTH legs — which is why the broker row reads `remarks=LMT_BOS_O: oco:26081…`. `backend/app/auto_live.py:585` journals `entry_price: float(ref_ltp)` from the same source.
ledger.failure: Every price in the PC-down safety net for the 2026-08-14 trade — trigger 21.45, limit 21.00, target 144.15/141.25 — was derived from a price the account never paid. The single seam `ref_ltp` feeds (1) the journal entry_price, (2) the guard's stop_level (30.68 instead of 30.85), and (3) all four OCO levels. On a wider entry slip (e.g. ref 61.35 / fill 75.00) the 'catastrophe' stop rests at 21.00 = 71% below the real cost basis, not 65%, and the guard's stop fires ~9 points early relative to actual risk. The reference-vs-fill error is systematic, not a one-off.
ledger.proposed_fix: `_transmit_and_arm` (`backend/app/live/executor.py:190-198`) already holds `result.norenordno` before it calls `arm(intent, result.norenordno)`. Fetch the broker `avgprc` (single_order_history / trade_book, both already on the client: `flattrade_client.py:223-229`, `:147-153`) and pass it to `arm` as an `entry_fill_price` argument. In `live_deploy_context._arm`, use `fill or ref_ltp` for BOTH `get_registry().register(entry_price=...)` (:152) and `compute_catastrophe_band(...)` (:174). One value, three consumers — do not fix the guard alone and leave the OCO band on the reference.
ledger.note: Reproduced: compute_catastrophe_band(61.35, guard_stop_pct=50) -> sl_limit 21.00 == the exact rejected price; from the fill 61.70 -> 21.10, absent from the order book. Forensic proof the rejected SELL was AlphaForge's own OCO stop leg, priced off the REFERENCE. Severity note: the band error is 0.10 (0.5%); the REJECTION cause was margin, not price.

ledger.title: A CREATED alert is treated as a WORKING backstop: nothing reads the OCO back, so a rejected leg is journalled as success
ledger.evidence: `backend/app/live_deploy_context.py:194-204` — the ONLY success test is `if res.get("ok")`. `res` comes from `FlattradeClient.place_oco` → `_post_alert` → `_parse_alert_response` (`backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:482-502`), where `ok = al_id is not None and stat != "not_ok"`. Per the decoded spec (`docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md:94-109`) the PlaceOCOOrder response carries ONLY `stat`/`request_time`/`al_id` — it says the ALERT was created and says nothing whatsoever about whether the order it will fire is placeable. `backend/app/auto_live.py:591-592` then writes `"oco_error": None if result.get("oco_al_id") else "no_broker_backstop"` — i.e. oco_error is null the instant any al_id comes back. `client.gtt_book()` (GetPendingGTTOrder, implemented at `flattrade_client.py:395-406`) is called ONLY from `reboot_reconcile.py:319` and the manual route `routers/live_broker.py:1344` — **never on the arm path**. `client.enabled_gtts()` (`flattrade_client.py:408-417`) is called from nowhere in `backend/app/`. The repo already owns the exact readback pattern for this failure mode: `kill_switch._scan_order_by_remarks` (`backend/app/live/kill_switch.py:713-746`) + `_REJECTED_STATUSES` (`:55`) used by `auto_square.py:698-710`, and `docs/DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md:657-658` names it ("broker can return an order# then async-REJECT it"). It was never applied to the OCO.
ledger.failure: 2026-08-14 exactly as observed: broker returned al_id 26081400000991, code recorded `oco_al_id="26081400000991", oco_error=null`, the AlertRail no-backstop banner (driven by `oco_error`, `live_blotter.py:175-182`) stayed silent, and the position ran with ZERO broker-side protection while every surface said it was protected. The failure is silent by construction: there is no code path in which a rejected/absent OCO leg can ever set `oco_error`.
ledger.proposed_fix: Add a readback immediately after the place, inside the SAME best-effort try/except (`live_deploy_context.py:193-217`) so it can never unwind a filled entry and adds no arming gate: (1) `rows = await client.gtt_book()`; require a row whose `al_id`/`Al_id` == the returned id AND whose `tsym`/`qty`/`prc` match what was sent; (2) scan `await client.order_book()` for any row whose `remarks` CONTAINS `oco:<norenordno>` and whose normalized status is in `_REJECTED_STATUSES` — reuse `kill_switch._normalize_status` (`:87`). On either miss, set `oco_al_id = None` and journal `oco_error="oco_not_resting"` / `f"oco_leg_rejected:{row.get('rejreason')}"`. Change `auto_live.py:592` to carry the specific reason string instead of deriving it from presence. Two read-only calls, ~15 lines, no new dependency.

ledger.title: reboot_reconcile compares an UPSTOX-space `trading_symbol` against a NOREN-keyed position book — it false-closes every live journal row and then cancels that row's still-resting OCO
ledger.evidence:
`backend/app/live/reboot_reconcile.py:143` does `tsym = str(doc.get("trading_symbol") or "")` and `:144` tests `if tsym in open_tsyms`, where `open_tsyms` is built at `:306`/`:58-75` from the broker `position_book`'s `row.get("tsym")` — Noren space.

`backend/app/auto_live.py:576-580` writes BOTH fields and labels the split explicitly: `"trading_symbol": contract_doc.get("trading_symbol")` with the comment "UPSTOX-space above; the broker's own symbol + segment below. Joining the two spaces is a long-standing source of real bugs here", and `"noren_tsym": result.get("tsym")`.

Three other call sites state the invariant this file violates:
- `backend/app/runtime.py:722-725`: "Ownership is resolved through the broker ORDER book, never by comparing live_trades.trading_symbol to the position book — that field is UPSTOX-space while the book is NOREN-keyed (the long-standing symbol-space invariant)."
- `backend/app/live/live_blotter.py:113-117`: "The position book is NOREN-keyed. `trading_symbol` is UPSTOX-space, so matching on it never succeeded" → uses `t.get("noren_tsym") or t.get("trading_symbol")`.
- `backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:600-603`: "Keyed on norenordno …, NEVER on trading_symbol — live_trades stores the UPSTOX symbol while the position book is NOREN-keyed."

This is not a boot-only path: `backend/app/runtime.py:1235-1242` re-runs `maybe_run_live_recovery()` from the supervisor loop until it reports complete, and `runtime.py:777-778` forces `complete=False` on every `unknown_position_book` pass — which is exactly the observed log shape (repeated "position_book empty/None" then one pass that closed the row).

Compounding: once phase 2 sets the doc CLOSED, phase 3 at `reboot_reconcile.py:257-261` finds `doc.get("status") == "CLOSED"` for the remarks-linked OCO and calls `client.cancel_oco(al_id)` — removing the PC-down backstop from a position the broker still holds.
ledger.failure:
Ran the real `reconcile_on_startup` against a HELD position (position_book `[{"tsym": "NIFTY18AUG26P24300", "netqty": "65"}]`) and a journal doc carrying `trading_symbol="NIFTY 18 AUG 26 24300 PE"` / `noren_tsym="NIFTY18AUG26P24300"`:

  summary        -> {'closed': 1, 'cancelled': 1, 'status': 'ok'}
  doc status     -> CLOSED reconciled_closed
  OCOs cancelled -> ['26081400000991']

The position is still 65 lots long at the broker. The journal says flat, and the resting OCO was cancelled. Today's trade only escaped the second half because its OCO was already dead.
ledger.proposed_fix: In `_reconcile_open_flat` use the same fallback `live_blotter.py:117` already uses — `tsym = str(doc.get("noren_tsym") or doc.get("trading_symbol") or "")` — and for a legacy doc with no `noren_tsym` do NOT close: `continue` with a `skipped_unknown_symbol_space` counter (fail closed; the current code fails open into a false close). Apply the same fix to the orphan-sweep query at `:266-268`, which must match `{"$or": [{"noren_tsym": tsym}, {"trading_symbol": tsym}]}`. Separately, refuse to CLOSE a row when `_match_exit_fill_price` returned None AND the tsym was never provably flat — write `status="NEEDS_REVIEW"` instead of CLOSED so an unproven close can never read as settled.

ledger.title: A wrongly-CLOSED journal row zeroes max_concurrent, the account-wide max_open_positions gate AND daily_loss_cap — a second real entry fires while the position is still open
ledger.evidence:
All three caps read the journal, and all three treat a CLOSED row as no exposure:
- `backend/app/live_deploy_governor.py:389-394` — `max_concurrent` counts only `str(row.get("status")).upper() == "OPEN"`.
- `backend/app/live_deploy_governor.py:94` + `:110-112` — the account gate's `open_count` / `account_max_open_block` likewise counts only OPEN rows.
- `backend/app/live_deploy_governor.py:184-185` — `open_unrealized_today` skips any row whose status is not OPEN, so the live −₹ MTM disappears.
- `backend/app/deployment_kill_switch.py:94-96` — `daily_realized_summary` includes the row (its `closed_at` is today) and adds `_float(trade.get("realized_pnl"))`; `_float(None)` returns `0.0` at `:32-38`. So the row contributes exactly ₹0.

The false close also converts a FAIL-CLOSED state into a fail-open one. While the row is OPEN with a stale/missing mark, `live_deploy_governor.py:188-193` sets `unknown=True` and `:362-367` refuses the entry with `exposure_unknown`. Once the row is CLOSED there are no OPEN rows at all, `unknown` is False, and the gate returns `allow: True`.

The periodic sweep is blinded identically — `evaluate_risk_supervision` at `:253-257` and `:287-291` uses the same two helpers.

The ONE cap that still holds is `max_lots_per_day`: `:376-380` counts by `_entered_today(row, today)` i.e. `created_at`, regardless of status, so the closed row's lots still count.
ledger.proposed_fix: Fix the root cause (finding 1) AND make the caps robust to it independently, since a broker-side external close can produce the same shape. In `open_unrealized_today` (`live_deploy_governor.py:183-196`) treat a row as UNKNOWN exposure — not settled — when it is CLOSED with `realized_pnl is None`: that combination is definitionally "we closed the journal without ever pricing the exit". `_reconcile_open_flat` already produces exactly that when `_match_exit_fill_price` returns None (`reboot_reconcile.py:149-158` passes `exit_price=None, fill_price=None`). A row that was never priced must make `unknown=True`, which routes to the existing `exposure_unknown` refusal at `:362-367` rather than to `allow: True`. Do the same in `evaluate_risk_supervision`.

ledger.title: Reconcile has no `seen_filled` / consecutive-flat-read gate — "absent from a non-empty book" is accepted as proof of flat on a single read, so a just-filled entry is eligible for an irreversible close
ledger.evidence:
`_reconcile_open_flat` (`backend/app/live/reboot_reconcile.py:136-164`) has exactly two gates before closing: the doc has a `norenordno`, and its symbol is not in `open_tsyms`. There is no check that the position was ever SEEN in the book, and no consecutive-read confirmation. `_open_tsyms`'s own docstring (`reboot_reconcile.py:58-64`) states the assumption plainly: "the caller treats a tsym missing from this map as flat — which is safe ONLY because the book was already confirmed to be a non-empty list". Non-empty is not the same as complete, and it is not the same as current.

The guard on the same broker data is far stricter (`backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:646-720`). It distinguishes never-seen from seen-then-gone via `seen_filled` (`:652`), holds a pending entry indefinitely on an UNKNOWN book (`:658-659`), holds on an unparseable netqty (`:701-705`), and only finalizes after N CONSECUTIVE authenticated flat reads (`:712-714`, default `flat_confirm_reads=2` at `:415`, `:497`) — with the rationale spelled out at `:706-711`: "a single flat read (broker book eventual-consistency blip ... a KNOWN book momentarily missing this row) can't un-watch a still-live position". Reconcile shares the destination (`close_live_trade`) but none of that evidence discipline, and its close is irreversible: `close_live_trade`'s `status != "CLOSED"` filter (`backend/app/live/close_loop.py:87`) makes the row permanently ineligible for re-open, so no later pass can undo it.

This matters independently of Finding 1 because of WHEN reconcile runs. It is not a boot one-shot: `runtime.py:777-778` forces `complete=False` on an unreadable book, `runtime.py:1240` retries it from the supervisor every tick, and `live_broker.py:512` forces a run on every OAuth callback. So it executes repeatedly during market hours, including in the seconds after a fill — precisely the window where Noren's position book has not yet published the new row.
ledger.failure: Entry fills at 09:20:03. The supervisor's retry pass runs at 09:20:05, before Noren publishes the row for that tsym, but the book is non-empty because a different position (or yesterday's netqty=0 row for another scrip) is present. `open_tsyms` does not contain the new tsym, so the brand-new position — which has never been seen in the book even once — is closed as `reconciled_closed` with realized_pnl=null. Same end state as today: caps and the day-stop go blind to a live position, and the row can never be reopened. A partial/eventually-consistent book that returns rows but omits this one produces the identical outcome at any point in the session.
ledger.proposed_fix:
State the rule explicitly and enforce it: a reconcile close must require positive, entry-specific evidence that the entry is terminal — never merely the absence of a row.

Require ALL of:
1. A KNOWN book — non-empty list (already enforced, `reboot_reconcile.py:300-304`). Keep it.
2. The doc's BROKER-space symbol resolved (Finding 1). No symbol -> no close.
3. Flat on N>=2 CONSECUTIVE passes. Reconcile is stateless across invocations, so persist the counter on the doc — `$inc` a `reconcile_flat_reads` field on a flat read and `$set` it to 0 on any held read; close only at >=2. This mirrors `live_position_guard._flat_confirm_reads` (`live_position_guard.py:712-714`) using the store reconcile already has.
4. Positive terminal evidence for THIS entry, one of:
   - a matched exit SELL fill — remarks `oco:<norenordno>`, or the existing unambiguous same-tsym fallback (`reboot_reconcile.py:89-115`) -> close WITH that price; or
   - the entry order is terminal-WITHOUT-fill — `order_book()` shows REJECTED/CANCELED for this `norenordno`, or today's trade book has no BUY fill for it -> close as `never_filled`, no P&L (this is the `seen_filled` analogue: an entry never seen filled has no position to close). `client.order_book()` is already available and used at `runtime.py:740`; or
   - the doc was created in a PRIOR IST session — today's trade book cannot carry yesterday's fill, so absence from today's non-empty book is genuine. This preserves the module's original overnight PC-down purpose.
   Otherwise -> UNKNOWN: leave the doc OPEN and log at WARNING.

Today's trade lands in the "otherwise" branch under this rule — same-day doc, confirmed BUY fill, no SELL fill anywhere, entry order not rejected — so it would have been held even if Finding 1 were unfixed. That is the property you asked for: the close cannot fire on a position that has never been proven to have left.

ledger.title: The software guard's entry basis is the pre-trade REFERENCE and nothing ever rebases it to the broker fill

The manual path has the identical defect at backend/app/routers/live_broker.py:362-363 and :376. ref_ltp is by its own definition a REFERENCE for BANDING the limit order, not a fill: backend/app/auto_live.py:20-22 says 'the live ENTRY ref_ltp must be [fresh] ... a stale ref_ltp would mis-band the live LMT', resolver at backend/app/auto_live.py:105.

NOTHING ever corrects it. Grep for entry_price in backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py returns only :197 (the register kwarg), :234 (the write), :1259 (basket premium read), and :1381/:1388 (the restart-only rehydrate_from_broker path). state["entry"] is written once in build_monitor_state (backend/app/live/live_sl_monitor.py:132) and never rewritten; the guard's cycle only ever mutates state via evaluate_exit (backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:764-765), which never touches "entry".

ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES THE LIVE EVIDENCE EXACTLY. resolve_premium_levels (backend/app/execution_policy.py:45-84, called with stop_floor=0.05, ndigits=2 at backend/app/live/live_sl_monitor.py:111-119): entry 61.35, stop_pct 50 -> stop_level 30.68, which is precisely the registered guard level. Off the true fill 61.70 it is 30.85.

THE FILL WAS THE LIMIT PRICE. order_builder computes eff = min(buffer_pct, band_pct) (backend/app/live/order_builder.py:262) then prc = round_to_tick(round(ref*(1+eff/100),2), tick, 'up') (:269-270). buffer_pct defaults to 0.5 (backend/app/live/executor.py:452, auto_live never overrides it) and band_pct to 5.0 (backend/app/live_deploy_context.py:44). round_to_tick(round(61.35*1.005,2),0.05,'up') = 61.70 -- exactly the broker avgprc. The 0.35 'slippage' IS the marketable cross buffer.

The same repo already fixed this asymmetry for MONEY but not for EXITS: backend/app/live/close_loop.py:103-111 explicitly prefers entry_fill_price over entry_price because 'entry_price is the pre-trade REFERENCE premium used to band the limit order -- an intent', and backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:616-624 says the same thing in the mark path. ledger.failure: On the 2026-08-14 trade: paid 61.70, guard stop set at 30.68 instead of 30.85. Real risk carried = 61.70 - 30.68 = 31.02/unit = 50.28% of premium, against a configured 50.00% (30.85/unit). Extra risk 0.17 x 65 = Rs 11.05. Bound on the basis error: the fill cannot exceed the LMT, so it is capped at ~0.5% + one tick above ref -- but the tick term dominates cheap options: 2.50% at a Rs 2 premium, 1.00% at Rs 5, 0.60% at Rs 25 (round_to_tick(round(P*1.005,2),0.05,'up')). Every per-position level -- stop, target, trailing trigger, lock level, peak seed -- is shifted by that amount, always in the adverse direction for a marketable buy.

ledger.title: Two same-direction SELL legs under ai_t=LMT_BOS_O is an UNDOCUMENTED configuration, and the trigger-direction rule is an explicit guess in our own comments

The decoded spec's only worked example (`docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md:65-90`) is leg1 `trantype:"B"` + leg2 `trantype:"S"` — a two-SIDED buy-or-sell OCO (consistent with the literal name LMT_B-O-S_O). The spec documents `oivariable.var_name` only as "x or y" (`:29`) and never states which var pairs with which leg, nor whether a trigger is above/below. Our own code admits this: `gtt.py:74-79` — "the broker infers above/below from each trigger value vs the LTP — so leg direction is value-driven, not x/y-labelled" — is an INFERENCE from two fired-leg remarks, not a spec statement; `CHANGELOG.md:1680-1682` records the same as "inferred from trigger-vs-LTP". If Noren instead treats x as an ABOVE trigger, then LTP 61.70 ≥ x=21.45 was already true at placement and leg 1 fires instantly — which is precisely what the order book shows (a SELL @21.00 submitted and rejected on the same day, with the observed remark carrying NO "Ltp X is below Y" suffix, unlike the June fired-leg remarks quoted at `gtt.py:76-78`). `enabled_gtts()` is never called, so it was never checked that this account even supports LMT_BOS_O.
ledger.failure: Either (a) the alert type is wrong for two same-direction legs and the broker rejects the leg on submission, or (b) the x-trigger is evaluated as 'above' and the stop leg fires immediately at entry — in which case, had it NOT been rejected, the OCO would have SOLD the whole 65-lot position at 21.00 seconds after buying it at 61.70, a ~₹2,600 instant loss. (3) Call `enabled_gtts()` once at connect and log the account's supported `ai_t` list; log-only, never a gate.
ledger.note: Built the intent and inspected it: leg1 trantype=S prc=21.00, leg2 trantype=S prc=141.25, with oivariable x=21.45 / y=144.15. Two SELL legs is the CORRECT bracket for a LONG option — both exits are sells, one triggering below and one above. The spec constrains trantype to B or S and does not require the legs to differ. The 2026-08-14 rejection was margin shortfall, proven in [3]/[4]; shape was never implicated.


ledger.title: jData is inserted into a form-urlencoded body without URL-encoding, contrary to the spec's explicit warning
ledger.evidence: `backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:98-100`: `return f"jData={json.dumps(jdata)}&jKey={self._jKey}"`, posted with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (`:111`). The decoded spec warns twice to URL-encode the symbol — `endpoints/04-place-order.md:22` and `endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md:20`: 'use url encoding to avoid special char error for symbols like M&M' — and `endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md:121` notes jData/jKey are a url-encoded form body. Any literal `&` in the payload truncates the body at that point; any literal `+` decodes as a space.
ledger.failure: Latent, not today's bug: NIFTY/SENSEX option tsyms and the `oco:<norenordno>` remark contain no `&` or `+`, so the 2026-08-14 payload transmitted intact. It bites the first time an operator-supplied remark, a strategy name, or an `&`-bearing symbol reaches any jData field — the broker then sees a silently truncated JSON object, whose most likely response is a generic 'Invalid Input' that gives no hint of the real cause.
ledger.proposed_fix: `from urllib.parse import urlencode` and return `urlencode({"jData": json.dumps(jdata), "jKey": self._jKey})`. One line, no behaviour change for today's payloads.
ledger.note: _make_body interpolated raw JSON into a form-urlencoded body. Latent (no '&' in index option tsyms or oco:<no> remarks) but real. Fixed 3222640 with urlencode(); 5 regressions; the client tests that sliced on a raw '&jKey=' now decode with parse_qs.

ledger.title: DETERMINATION: the fill is NOT knowable at arm time — Noren PlaceOrder does not return it; it first becomes knowable ~1.5s later on the guard's first position-book cycle
ledger.evidence:
NOT KNOWABLE AT ARM. OrderResult carries only ok / norenordno / rejreason / raw -- backend/app/live/broker_protocol.py:96-101. That is not an app omission: the Noren PlaceOrder RESPONSE DETAILS table lists exactly stat, request_time, norenordno -- docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/04-place-order.md:64-78, with the sample success response showing only those three keys (:71-78). backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:284-289 therefore has nothing further to carry. Note the doc's own caveat at :69: norenordno 'will be present only on successful Order placement to OMS' -- an ACCEPT, not a fill. The codebase is built on that premise: the registry seeds seen_filled=False with a miss counter (backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:250-252) precisely because 'a just-armed position may not be in the position book yet', and backend/app/runtime.py:257-262 records that 'a marketable LMT the market walks away from never fills'. So registering ref_ltp in arm() is not a mistake of omission -- it is the only number in existence at that instant. The defect is purely that nothing corrects it afterwards.

WHERE THE FILL LIVES. Three reachable sources: (1) SingleOrdHist (#12) returns avgprc = 'Average trade price of total traded quantity' plus fillshares and status/rpt -- docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/endpoints/12-single-order-history.json, sample row {"status":"COMPLETE","rpt":"Fill","avgprc":"800.00"}. The client method EXISTS at backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:223-229 and has ZERO production callers (grep across backend/ returns only the definition). (2) OrderBook (#10) also carries avgprc/fillshares. (3) PositionBook's daybuyavgprc, which the guard ALREADY reads every ~1.5s and already extracts at backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:629.

What is NOT available: the WebSocket order-update path. order_sm.apply_om parses avgprc correctly (backend/app/live/order_sm.py:370-381) but its only entrypoint engine.on_om (backend/app/live/engine.py:118) has no production subscriber -- grep finds only the mock and the client-side WS helper (backend/app/live/flattrade_client.py:440,475,527), never a caller that starts it. backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:622-624 states this in the source.
ledger.failure: N/A -- this is the determination the fix depends on, not a defect. It rules OUT the tempting fix ('have the executor return avgprc from place_order and pass it to arm') as impossible against this broker API, and rules IN the cheap one.
ledger.proposed_fix: ANSWER: the fill first becomes knowable on the guard's FIRST cycle that finds this position in the position book -- the cycle that sets entry["seen_filled"] = True at backend/app/live/live_position_guard.py:723, roughly 1.5 s after arm (POLL_SECONDS = 1.5, :62), with the row `pos` already bound at :647 and daybuyavgprc already being read at :629. It costs ZERO additional broker calls: the value is already fetched, already extracted, already written to Mongo as entry_fill_price via backend/app/runtime.py:230-251 (which is where the journal's 61.70 / 61.35 / 0.35 came from), and then discarded in memory. SingleOrdHist would be marginally earlier and exact-per-order rather than per-contract-per-day, but costs an extra call, needs a fresh polling loop that does not exist, and is not guaranteed to be COMPLETE inside the arm call -- so it is the wrong trade for this fix. Use the position book. Do not add a new gate, a new arming condition, or any order-placing behaviour: the change is confined to a read path plus one kwarg on register().
ledger.note: Correct and confirmed against the spec: PlaceOrder returns only stat/request_time/norenordno (endpoints/04-place-order.md:64-78), so ref_ltp at arm is the only number in existence — not an omission. The gap was that nothing corrected it AFTERWARDS; closed by b3f7df3 (trailing anchor) and cfe1c25 (basket notional), both using the daybuyavgprc the guard already reads at ~1.5s. Side-finding worth keeping: client.single_order_history() exists with ZERO production callers, and the WS order-update path (order_sm.apply_om) has no subscriber — both are latent capability.

ledger.title: Enumeration: every Flattrade endpoint that could provide a resting protective exit, per the decoded spec
ledger.evidence: From docs/Resources/flattrade-pi-api/ (58 endpoints, vision-verified). (1) **POST /PlaceOCOOrder** (#21, endpoints/21-place-oco-order.md) — requires uid, tsym, exch, validity(DAY|GTT), ai_t, plus BOTH `place_order_params` and `place_order_params_leg2` full order blocks (`:26-27`) and an `oivariable` array of {d, var_name:x|y} compared against LTP (`:28-29`). Each leg requires tsym/exch/trantype(B|S)/prctyp/prd/ret(DAY|EOS|IOC)/actid/uid/qty/prc; `trgprc` only 'in case of SL-LMT' (`:42`). Success `stat:"OI created"` + `al_id`; failure `stat:"Not_Ok"` + `emsg` limited to 'Invalid Input' or 'Session Expired' (`:96-101`) — **the response says nothing about the fired leg**. Documented sample is a two-SIDED B+S pair (`:65-90`); the doc's own ai_t literal is `LMT_BOS_O`, which is where that string in the rejection comes from — it is OUR alert type echoed back, not evidence of a BO/CO product. (2) **POST /PlaceGTTOrder** (#16) — single leg, FLAT form: uid/tsym/exch/ai_t/validity/d/remarks/trantype/prctyp/prd/ret/actid/qty/prc/dscqty (`endpoints/16-place-gtt-order.md:16-33`). Restrictions: `prctyp` ∈ LMT|SL-LMT|DS|2L|3L (`:27`), `prd` ∈ **C|M|H only** (`:28` — no I/MIS, no B/BO), `ret` ∈ DAY|EOS|IOC, dscqty required. Success `stat:"Oi created"` + **`Al_id`** (capital A, `:63-71`). (3) **/ModifyGTTOrder #17, /CancelGTTOrder #18, /GetPendingGTTOrder #19, /ModifyOCOOrder #22, /CancelOCOOrder #23** — lifecycle only; GetPendingGTTOrder returns the resting book WRAPPED (derived oivariable + place_order_params, `endpoints/19-get-pending-gtt-order.md:51-80`), which is a READ shape, not the write contract. (4) **/GetEnabledGTTs #20** and **/GetEnabledAlertTypes #40** — both return `ai_ts:[{ai_t:…}]`; the doc samples list only base codes ATP/LTP/'Perc. Change' (`endpoints/20-get-enabled-gtts.md:39-48`), so treat them as advisory, never as a gate. (5) **/SetAlert #36, /ModifyAlert #38, /CancelAlert #37, /GetPendingAlert #39** — NOTIFICATION ONLY: SetAlert's jData is uid/tsym/exch/ai_t/validity/d/remarks with no trantype, qty or prc (`endpoints/36-set-alert.md:16-26`). These cannot exit a position. (6) **/PlaceOrder #4 with prctyp=SL-LMT** — supported by the spec (`endpoints/04-place-order.md:29`, trgprc at `:25`) but ruled OUT empirically: a resting SELL stop on a long option margin-rejects (docs/STRATEGY_DEPLOYMENTS.md:347-350, 'proven live 2026-06-24'). Note the spec lists no SL-M/market type at all — `prctyp` is LMT|SL-LMT. (7) **/PlaceOrder with bpprc/blprc/trailprc** (BO/CO brackets, `:33-35`, prd B/H at `:27`) — ruled OUT: CLAUDE.md and the Flattrade MCP server instructions both state BO and CO are NOT supported via the API. (8) **/ExitSNOOrder #7** — exits an existing special-order leg; not a resting protective exit.
ledger.failure: Answering the operator's question (a) directly: YES, a protective resting exit is genuinely placeable — but only through the GTT family (#16 or #21), and the intent AlphaForge builds is SHAPE-valid per #21 (every required field is present and every enum value is legal) while being SEMANTICALLY unverified in exactly one respect: two same-direction SELL legs with an inferred x/y→direction rule. Answering (b): NO, the rejection was NOT detectable at place time — by spec the PlaceOCOOrder response carries only stat/request_time/al_id, and a leg rejection surfaces later in the ORDER BOOK; the code inspects only the place response.
ledger.proposed_fix: Adopt #16 (single-leg PlaceGTTOrder, ai_t=LTP_B_O) as the protective exit and add the order-book/gtt-book readback — see the two findings above for exact payloads and call sites.
